blurb: Muscular American farm and ranch bulldog revived from near extinction after WWII
description: The American Bulldog is a large, muscular mastiff-type dog from the United States with a short, smooth coat, descended from Old English farm bulldogs.
answer: The American Bulldog is a large, muscular mastiff-type breed developed in the United States from the Old English Bulldog. Its ancestors worked on small farms and ranches as guardians, stock dogs and catch dogs. Most weigh between about 27 and 54 kg and stand 52 to 70 cm at the withers.

body: Like the English Bulldog, the American Bulldog descends from the Old English Bulldog. Bulldogs reached the British North American colonies as working dogs, used for guarding farms, handling stock and catching cattle; in England they had also been used in bull-baiting, which Britain banned in 1835. American dogs were bred for temperament and work rather than bloodline. After World War II the type nearly died out, and John D. Johnson and Alan Scott are widely credited with saving it, producing the Bully or Johnson type and the Standard or Scott type. The United Kennel Club recognized the breed in 1999, and it entered the AKC Foundation Stock Service in 2019.

The American Bulldog is stocky and heavily built, with a large head and muscular shoulders and forearms. The short, smooth coat was historically mostly white with red, black or brindle patches and now comes in many colors. Bully types are larger with shorter muzzles; Standard types are more athletic, with longer muzzles. Many modern dogs mix both types.
The available sources say little about temperament beyond the breed's history as a utilitarian farm dog selected for working ability. Prospective owners are best guided by breed club descriptions.

The coat needs little maintenance beyond an occasional bath, and the breed is a light to moderate shedder. American Bulldogs are known to drool more than many breeds. Sources give little detail on exercise, though as a muscular working breed it is generally expected to need regular activity.

Conditions reported in the breed include neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis, allergic skin disease, ichthyosis, solar dermatosis, squamous cell carcinoma and juvenile-onset demodicosis. Breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: How big does an American Bulldog get?
faq.a: Most weigh about 27 to 54 kg and stand 52 to 70 cm at the withers, though some non-standard dogs exceed this.

faq.q: How long do American Bulldogs live?
faq.a: A typical lifespan of about 10 to 15 years is commonly listed.
They are light to moderate shedders with a short, smooth coat that needs little maintenance, but they tend to drool more than many breeds.

faq.q: Is the American Bulldog the same as the American Bully?
faq.a: No. The American Bully is a separate breed developed from the American Pit Bull Terrier and several bulldog breeds, recognized by the UKC in 2013.
